A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same empirical study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA and object-property prediction experiments, including model comparisons and supplementary analyses in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised synthetic-dataset baseline results in Figures 2 and 15.

M1.justification: The representation-learning framework, text encoder, representation formatting, downstream transformer, and training objectives are unchanged. The revision concerns a comparison baseline rather than the study's main method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CLEVR6, CLEVRTex, Multi-dSprites, and the same filtered VQA-v2 subset. VQA and object-property prediction task coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Section 3.2 and Figures 2 and 15 replace the synthetic datasets' majority-class baseline with a trained question-only predictor. VQA-v2 already used a question-only baseline in v1. The representation-model comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Synthetic evaluations now control for prediction from question text through a learned question-only model, rather than constant majority-class prediction. Splits, preprocessing, metrics, and the retained models' training budgets and size configurations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The question-only comparison extends the assessment of performance without visual input to the synthetic datasets. Existing property-prediction correlations, upstream-metric analyses, model-size and data-size sweeps, question-category analyses, and extended VAE training experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same seed-count disclosures, 95% confidence-interval reporting, and correlation significance practices. No increase in repeated runs or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 15 replaces the 26.8% majority-class baseline at every Multi-dSprites size with question-only accuracies of 55.4%, 56.1%, 55.9%, and 57.2% for 40k, 80k, 160k, and 320k images, respectively. Figure 2 also updates synthetic baseline bars. These are different comparators, not same-model performance gains; representation-model results in Tables 7–13 and the VQA-v2 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of representations and downstream prediction is unchanged. Neither version adds or revises theoretical propositions, proofs, or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about foundation-model performance, downstream compute trade-offs, and the benefits of combining foundation models with object-centric representations.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds a qualification to the usefulness of several models on CLEVR and CLEVRTex: their performance barely exceeds prediction from questions alone. Existing limitations concerning synthetic data and differing foundation-model pretraining remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices B–D retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing instructions, and resource information. No dedicated architecture or training details are added for the revised synthetic baseline.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Dittadi and Winther's LAVAE and Daniel and Tamar's work on deep latent particles, expanding the bibliography from 96 to 98 references. The research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to the baseline description, synthetic-results discussion, real-world-results paragraph, and acknowledgments. The section structure and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Local spacing and text wrapping change around the results discussion, and the expanded bibliography reflows. All figure and table structures are retained; the updated baseline bars do not introduce new chart designs.

improvement.justification: Replacing majority-class prediction with question-only baselines makes the synthetic comparisons more informative about the contribution of visual representations. Section 4.1 appropriately acknowledges that several models barely outperform text alone. This strengthens the evaluation modestly, while the main results remain unchanged and baseline-specific implementation details are not expanded.
